bounds.domain: Two immutable original object keys, one deletion root and two lease generations. Successful idempotent delete, lost replies, takeover and cursor acknowledgement are separate transitions.
bounds.atomicity: Final SQL publication atomically retains all original manifests in v2 job.data and marks app metadata deleted. Small result cursors require original live job lease; v2 job/org deletion waits for cleanup confirmation. Legacy v1 jobs retain prior semantics and may have orphan debt.
bounds.conformance: Twenty-three real PGlite object/service cases and ten PostgreSQL cases, including independent connection contention, job/org cascade protection and post-lock expiry in UTC, New York and Kathmandu. Provider effects are local controlled fixtures. Real React table/settings/page/query-cache/HTTP-client tests cover two pending rows, disabled mutation controls and receipt-gated removal. Refetched metadata absence cannot remove an owned pending row; actual page and separate user/org-keyed remount tests reject late publication into a new authority. Three actual-detail-page cases retain pending metadata and reject late completion after user or organization retirement. Deletion navigation and scoped list updates require the original mounted owner. Twelve actual-client cases require cleanup confirmation and retain accepted original job identity through deadline, cancellation and transport loss. Nineteen UI cases include six actual detail/list recovery paths that retain pending rows and resume with GET only; confirmed terminal failure is displayed as requiring recovery.
bounds.gaps: Assumes original R2 binding and immutable deployment-key ownership remain stable; no live R2, bucket rotation, remote atomicity, arbitrary-count proof or general TypeScript refinement is established. A timed-out in-flight exact-key delete may finish after lease loss. Complete plans intentionally remain inline and immutable in job.data, with small independently updated result receipts. Physical PostgreSQL write-cost measurements are experimental evidence, not a worst-case bound. Uploads bind their complete plan before PUT; deletion waits for the original writer to acknowledge all issued PUTs and stop issuing more. Ambiguous legacy/failed uploads remain typed recovery-required; no elapsed-time quiescence or automatic unknown-PUT recovery is claimed. UI projection is one row of the local deletion set; no general React refinement or native-device claim. UI batch admission is serialized by one synchronous ref; this models two local batch attempts, not cancellation of server jobs. The detail snapshot is local to one mounted user/organization/app owner; a browser reload does not restore it or cancel the server job. The observation model starts after a validated accepted job identity; a lost initial DELETE response before a job ID arrives remains a separate admission-reconciliation boundary.
bounds.progress: Progress requires eventual provider/SQL availability, retained original queue, fair scheduling, and a successful acknowledged attempt before bounded no-progress retries exhaust. This safety model does not prove temporal liveness. Forward progress resets the bounded retry counter; one invocation handles at most 64 objects.
